sentences.text: Patagotitan was a massive quadrupedal herbivore defined by its exceptionally long neck and tail.
Scientists distinguish this species from its relatives through unique characteristics found in its vertebrae, shoulder bones, forelimb bones, and hindlimb bones.
The name combines a reference to Patagonia with the Greek word for Titan to reflect the creature's immense strength and large size.
It possessed a robust and expanded scapula blade that was only 4.15 times longer than it was wide at its narrowest point.
The front and middle neck vertebrae of Patagotitan were extremely long, at least five times longer than they were wide at the rear.
Later research revised Patagotitan's size to approximately 31 meters in length and 50 to 60 tonnes in weight.
Researchers claim Patagotitan would be the largest land animal of all time.
Researchers described Patagotitan as the largest known land animal based on bone sizes exceeding previous giants.
The genus Patagotitan was described by Carballido and colleagues in 2017.
A partial lower femur was discovered in 2010 by a farm laborer near La Flecha, Argentina.
Skeletal mounts of Patagotitan are displayed in multiple museums.
Patagotitan lived in a forested floodplain environment dominated by coniferous trees.
Patagotitan lived in a forested region.
A new genus of cypress, Austrocupressinoxylon, was named in 2019 from fossilized wood found near Patagotitan.
The fossilized cypress trees found near Patagotitan were estimated to be 15.3 meters tall.
Fossilized tree trunks and plant impressions show that Patagotitan lived in a lush forest with trees up to 15 meters tall, contrasting with today's dry landscape.
Sediments containing Patagotitan fossils indicate low-energy water flow on a floodplain.
Flooding was likely too weak to move Patagotitan bones, meaning the individuals were preserved where they died.
The expanded transverse processes on Patagotitan's tail vertebrae provided larger muscle attachment areas, resulting in a more muscular tail.
Patagotitan is classified within the family Lognkosauria.
A 2017 analysis placed Patagotitan as the sister group to Argentinosaurus.
Patagotitan was used in the re-definition of the group Colossosauria in 2022.
Patagotitan lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Albian stage.
The rock layers containing Patagotitan fossils are dated to approximately 101.62 million years ago.
Fossils of Patagotitan were found in the Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
Gregory S. Paul argued in 2019 that Patagotitan could not have been larger than Argentinosaurus because its back vertebrae were significantly shorter.
The evolutionary relationships of titanosaurs have historically been unstable and varied between analyses.
Scientific writer Riley Black warned in 2014 that it was too early to make size estimates with the desired scientific certainty.
